findings.summary: A stale build artifact in the verifier's shared target dir breaks a debug-profile test build; this is about the environment, not the candidate.
findings.evidence: `cargo test --locked -p athena-cli --test slot_exec` failed with E0432 `no CargoShim in env`, although git status is clean and env.rs:212 defines it. athena-agent was not recompiled. The likeliest cause is Athena's reverted scratch build, which shares the same artifact paths with older source mtimes. Rebuilding under --release passed. This is about the snapshot environment only: the candidate's own CI run passed.

findings.summary: Any later command leaves the wait note in place, so the job is held even if the producer moved on.
findings.evidence: Only a later slot acquisition clears the note. If the producer gives up on one `cargo build`, then does other work such as `cargo fmt`, and ends with work that may be fine, the job is still held and the producer's spend is paid again on retry. The design doc documents this and it is a conservative choice. A simpler alternative would hold only when the producer reports it could not build.

findings.summary: If the wrapper is SIGKILLed, the slot frees while the child cargo may still be running.
findings.evidence: The documented trade-off: the child is not exec'd because the workspace denies unsafe. The design doc names it and relies on the Bash timeout and kill switch to end the process group.

summary: The retry fixes the earlier job's blocker and its other findings. `athena-cli --test slot_exec` is registered in xtask/shard-timings.txt and the shard guard passes. The fmt/metadata no-slot test is present, the previously unlisted files are now deliverables, and the design doc explains the argv[0] dispatch. I read the full diff and ran the targeted tests, all of which passed: the 5 slot_exec integration tests (real athena binary linked as `cargo`, real SlotQueue, fake cargo), 19 policy tests, 5 env shim tests, the 2 new core tests, and the xtask guard. They show four behaviours. A second producer cargo queues while the first holds the only slot, then runs. Commands with leading global flags (`-q build`, `--locked test`) hold a slot and free it after. A wait past the limit exits 75 with the documented message, never starts cargo, and the job is held as `environment: build slot wait`. fmt/metadata/tree take no slot. CARGO_GLOBAL_FLAGS is the single list, shared through one walk. Only the producer's PATH gets the shim, and the verifier, reader and `env::build` environments are unchanged. The fmt, clippy and full-test results are taken from Athena's CI record. One environment note: a debug-profile build in this snapshot hit a stale athena-agent artifact, apparently left by Athena's reverted scratch build, so I ran the targeted tests with --release. Every file changed is on the deliverables list, and no governance file or records/ path is touched. My findings are minor or nit, none blocking.
